subject: Console error budget MVP scope + rollout integration timeline
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 2:32 PM PST
Subject: Console error budget MVP scope + rollout integration timeline

Hi Ethan + Sean,

Following up on yesterday’s sync and to close the loop on PM-612: below is the proposed MVP scope for Console error budget views + how it connects to rollout tooling (warn-only first). Please reply-all with any concerns by EOD tomorrow so we can lock for Chloe’s sprint planning.

Goals for MVP (Console):
1) Make tier context obvious (Hosted vs Dedicated), and show “budget remaining” + burn in a way that oncall and release owners can act on.
2) Keep permissions safe by default (no cross-customer leakage for Dedicated), and keep the first release internal.
3) Align timing with rollout gates so users see the same “source of truth” status in Console and in canary/deploy screens.

MVP scope (what we WILL ship):
A) Error budget overview page (internal)
- Primary grouping: Tier (Hosted/Dedicated) → Service (gateway/routing/runtime/control-plane) → Region.
- For each row: budget remaining (30d), current burn status (OK / At Risk / Exhausted), and a sparkline for burn rate.
- Standard windows displayed: 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d burn.
- Click-through takes you to the SLO dashboard + SRE runbook link.

B) Detail page
- Show SLO target, SLI definition pointer (Confluence link), and time series for the SLI.
- Overlay “recent changes” (deploys + config changes) pulled from the rollout/change feed (even if the rollout gate is warn-only).

C) Rollout integration (UI + API contract)
- Rollout UI shows a read-only badge: “Error budget: OK / At Risk / Exhausted” for the scoped service+tier+region.
- No hard blocking in MVP. The gate continues to be warn-only, but the UI should match the same computed status.
- We will include a link from the rollout screen back to the Console detail page.

D) Permissions model (MVP)
- Internal only for MVP.
- Access controlled by existing Console RBAC role: “reliability_viewer” (same as SLO dashboards).
- Dedicated: show only aggregated internal views (no per-customer dedicated pool pages in MVP).

Explicitly OUT of scope for MVP (future follow-ups):
- Customer-facing Dedicated budget views (requires per-customer scoping + a review with Security/Support).
- Per-model breakdowns in Console (we can link out to Grafana/our dashboards; we won’t build model slicing UI yet).
- Budget forecasting (“time to exhaustion”) beyond the burn-rate panels.
- Approval/override flows in Console (override token workflow remains in CI for now; we can show that an override occurred as an event).

Proposed timeline (to align with ENG-2422 / warn-only gates):
- By Feb 27: Agree on API response shape for “budget status” (control plane endpoint + fields needed for UI).
- Week of Mar 2: Console MVP pages behind feature flag; wired to staging budget status.
- Week of Mar 16: Rollout UI badge integration in staging + dogfood.
- End of Mar: Ship to internal prod (feature flagged), then expand access.

Open questions I need Eng/SRE confirmation on:
1) Canonical ownership labels: should “service” be control-plane/gateway/routing/runtime only, or do you want more granularity (e.g., scheduler)?
2) Dedicated scope: for MVP we’re not doing per-customer. Is tier-level aggregated Dedicated acceptable for SRE/oncall workflows?
3) Burn thresholds: can we treat “At Risk / Exhausted” as whatever the policy defines (multi-window burn), without re-encoding logic in Console?

If you’re aligned, I’ll update the design/spec page and ask Chloe to execute starting next sprint.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


---
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 4:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Console error budget MVP scope + rollout integration timeline

+1 on the MVP shape.

On your questions:
1) Keep “service” coarse for MVP (gateway / routing / runtime / control-plane). We can add sub-service tags later, but it will complicate the API and the RBAC story.
2) Aggregated Dedicated is fine for MVP. The per-customer view is the hard part (authZ + data model). Let’s not pull it in.
3) Yes—Console should treat status as an output of the policy engine/budget computation. We’ll expose a single status enum + the raw burn rates per window.

We can have a draft API response for the budget-check endpoint by Feb 27. I’ll ask Benji to include the fields you listed (status, remaining, burn_1h/6h/24h/7d, last_updated).

Ethan

Ethan Park
Engineering Manager, Control Plane
Redwood Inference


---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 5:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Console error budget MVP scope + rollout integration timeline

Aligned.

A couple SRE asks for MVP:
- Please ensure the detail page always links to the canonical SLO definition (Confluence) AND the runbook for budget exhaustion response. We’ve had too many “pretty graphs, no actions.”
- For streaming, we should be careful in naming: latency is TTFT vs stream duration; disconnect rate is separate. Console can stay generic in MVP (“Latency SLI” with link), but avoid implying a single number applies to streaming.
- “At Risk / Exhausted” must be computed from the policy (multi-window burn). We don’t want per-team interpretations.

Dedicated aggregated view is still useful for oncall, so I’m good with that for now.

Sean

Sean Gallagher
Director of Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 9:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Console error budget MVP scope + rollout integration timeline

Thanks both.

I’ll update the design/spec page today with:
- Service list (coarse for MVP)
- Required links (SLO definition + runbook)
- Copy guidance for streaming (avoid oversimplifying TTFT vs duration)

Also confirming: MVP is internal-only + feature flagged; customer-facing Dedicated is a separate follow-up (we’ll loop Support/Security when we pick that up).

Marissa
